findings.title: Fallback chain crashes on nil default locale and hits DB on every lookup
findings.body: FallbackLocaleList#[] builds [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact. to_sym is called before compact, so if SiteSetting.default_locale is nil (unseeded DB, test setup, migration) it raises NoMethodError instead of falling back to :en. Worse, this method is called by I18n::Backend::Fallbacks on every I18n.t to compute the fallback chain, so every translation now triggers a SiteSetting (DB/cached-setting) read and any DB outage or early-boot call (migrations, asset precompile, console, initializers) breaks all translations.

findings.title: LRU translation cache ignores site default locale, serves stale fallback
findings.body: I18n.translate caches with key "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}", which includes only key and current locale. With the new fallback order of user locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, then :en, the result for the same key+locale changes when the admin changes the site default locale. The cache is never invalidated on that change, so after a default-locale change users keep receiving the previously cached fallback language until entries are evicted or the process restarts.

findings.title: Fallback locale files only preloaded in controller, missing elsewhere
findings.body: I18n.translate only calls load_locale(config.locale) for the current locale, while preloading of the full fallback chain (current locale, site default, :en) only happens in ApplicationController#set_locale via I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. Because translations are loaded lazily on demand, any I18n.t outside a web request (Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks, console) or any I18n.t with an explicit locale: option can resolve to a fallback locale whose YAML was never loaded, so lookup returns translation-missing even though the translation exists on disk.
